key_insight: SAGE-PINN builds an axisymmetric PINN that removes cylindrical-coordinate singularities by using a parity-preserving variable transformation and physics-aware architecture, enabling stable multiphysics flow prediction without labeled data.
engineering_relevance: It offers a mesh-free surrogate for stenosed-artery nanofluid flow and heat transfer in cylindrical geometries, which is useful for biomedical flow analysis and other axisymmetric CFD applications.
method: Uses s = r^2 and a modified stream-function form to eliminate explicit 1/r singular terms and enforce mass conservation exactly.
Encodes boundary conditions analytically and trains in stages for momentum, thermal, and coupled physics residuals.
Stabilizes optimization with residual normalization, Péclet-/Richardson-number continuation, and a physics-scaled drift guard.
evidence_signal: Validated against finite-element reference solutions with no labeled training data; mass conservation stayed at single-precision round-off, and central-range errors were about 1.6% for axial velocity and 9.1% for temperature.
watch_item: Performance degrades in extreme regimes, especially strongly buoyancy-influenced slow flow and highly advection-dominated heat transfer, so those cases may need extra care or tuning.
paper_title: SAGE-PINN: A Singularity-free Axisymmetric Geometry-Encoded Physics-Informed Neural Network for Axisymmetric Multiphysics Flow in Cylindrical Coordinates
